sample_unit: LLM responses (5 models x 4 questions x 3 runs)

links.outcome: Rated safety, completeness and accuracy of LLM answers to patient neurointerventional questions
links.effect: Median safety >4 on 5-point scale, suggesting low risk of overtly harmful advice, but responses were often incomplete or imprecise; physicians rated more critically than non-physicians.
links.quote: Recent-generation LLMs offer medically safe, though often incomplete or imprecise, information in response to patient-oriented neurointerventional queries.

unlisted_practices: Including lay (non-physician) raters alongside physicians when evaluating LLM outputs
Plagiarism analysis of LLM-generated patient information

screen.reason: The study evaluates five commercial LLMs on patient-facing neurointerventional clinical queries using multirater evaluations (accuracy, completeness, safety, actionability), but does not test an organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
